facts: CONTINUATION IS DERIVED, NOT EMITTED. Whether the person went back to work is the next user turn within 10 minutes of `break_closed`, computed in APL from turn events that already exist. Emitting a "resumed" event would ask the client to observe something it has no reliable view of.
a break ended. A CLOSED vocabulary, like the census codes: these are a histogram dimension and an open set would let a new renderer widen the cardinality of the field the whole readout groups on.

- `x`, the explicit dismiss control. - `continue`, the affirmative "I'm done reading" button. - `escape`, a keyboard dismiss. Deliberately NOT pooled with `x`: one is a considered exit and one is a reflex, and telling them apart is how a format learns whether it is being read or swatted.

eli5.text: The SPOTLIGHT ad card now measures how long it keeps you from quickly closing it. When that ad pops up, the X, the backdrop, and Escape key stay locked for up to 5 seconds so you can't slip away immediately, but the sponsor's link stays clickable the whole time so you always have a way out through the advertiser. This lock timing is tracked separately from the countdown timer on the regular Intermission card, because tuning one format used to silently change the other. Operators can now turn the lock off completely (drop it to zero seconds) without pushing out new software, and the data will show whether people waited out the lock and bounced or instead clicked through while it was still held.

eli5.text: If you use the Freebuff helper tool on the command line, you will now see how long until your daily pool of free uses refills, shown in days and hours instead of just a raw counter. This update also makes the tool handle retry waits in a friendlier day-scale format and carry forward Freebucks balance when it shows you a refusal message. The version label was bumped to mark this release, which is live now as part of the standard update channel.
